ben_perf: FYI ran a couple nsys timelines against the 8k-workload and saw weird interleaving between 'attn_kv' and 'softmax' kernels across requests. attaching screenshot and .qdrep soon :eyes:
maria_runtime: can you share the command + cfg you used? curious about batch sizes and kvcache enabled/disabled
ben_perf: ran `nsys profile -t cuda,osrt -o perf_8k --trace-fork-before-exec true ./serve --batch=8 --max-seqlen=8192 --kvcache=on`
jordan_ml: if kvcache is warm we expect heavy kernel reuse; interleaving might be from continuous-batching trying to pack tails. what's the per-request nvtx layout?
ben_perf: currently NVTX only wraps high-level request -> `NVTX_RANGE_PUSH("request")` in serve loop, nothing per-kernel. profiler shows contiguous kernels but ranges collapse, so it's hard to map which kernel is for which request
alex_infra: hmm, we've discussed adding per-request spans earlier. downside: too many NVTX ranges can blow up trace size and slow profiling. we should pick a naming scheme and granularity.
maria_runtime: proposal: keep coarse `request/<model>@<ver>` plus optional `op/<op_type>` inside the runtime. example: `request/llama2-70b@v2` then `op/kv_lookup`, `op/attn_fwd`, `op/softmax`. that gives mapping w/o per-token spam
jordan_ml: I like that. Also include a short request id suffix (4 chars) for grouping when multiple requests interleave. e.g., `request/llama2-70b@v2#1a2f`
ben_perf: ok example NVTX usage I'd add in runtime before kernel launch: ```cpp
NVTX_RANGE_PUSH_FMT("op=%s req=%s model=%s ver=%s", op_name, req_short, model, ver);
launch_kernel(...);
NVTX_RANGE_POP();
```
alex_infra: can we standardize op_name values? we'll need mapping to kernel selectors: `kv_lookup`, `kv_apply_cache`, `kv_serialize`, `attn_fwd`, `attn_apply_rot`, `softmax`, `gelu`, `matmul_fused` etc. keep them short and snake_case
maria_runtime: also recommend tagging batching decisions: `batch/size=8` at the request span root and if continuous-batching creates a merged unit, emit `batch/merged=true` span around the combined launch. helps explain why multiple requests share kernels in trace
jordan_ml: regarding trace overhead: sample a run with NVTX only for request boundaries vs request+op and compare qdrep size + nsys cpu overhead. we should add an automated bench in perf-suite that runs 1k synthetic short requests and measures latency + trace size
perf-bot: @ben_perf created perf run tracker: PR#4213 and results job 17685 queued. link: https://perf.redwood/bench/17685
ben_perf: will add kvcache-disable run and a warm-cache run, then attach qdrep diffs. next step: agree on op name list and short id format, i'll draft a small RFC and instrument a branch for perf comparisons :thumbsup:
maria_runtime: sounds good. can we also include a convention for kernel-level NVTX when we call device kernels directly from runtime (e.g., `nvtx:kernel:attn_qk`)? keep that separate namespace to avoid collisions
alex_infra: agreed. namespace idea: `req:` for high level, `op:` for runtime ops, `k:` for kernel-level. e.g., `req/llama2-70b#1a2f`, `op/attn_fwd`, `k/attn_qk_kernel_v3`
jordan_ml: looks solid. add it to the runtime tracing README and we'll iterate after we see perf numbers. thanks everyone
ben_perf: thanks — I'll post the qdrep links and RFC in this thread when ready
perf-bot: perf run 17685 finished: artifacts at https://perf.redwood/bench/17685/artifacts (qdrep, summary.csv)
